#2. residual variances observed variables
rp1 ~~ rp1

> Hedonic_Risk ~~ Hedonic_Risk
> Selfimage_Risk ~~ Selfimage_Risk
> womr ~~ womr"

First some notes about your syntax: since your are using the
'user-friendly' sem() function, there is no need to specify the residual
variances of the observed variables, nor the variances of the latent
factors; so you can remove section 2 and 3 from your syntax.

> I got this warning message as following:
>
> Error in solve.default(E) :
> system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number =
> 2.44603e-24
> Warning message:
> In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options =
> lavaanOptions, :
> lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

This is typically a symptom that your model is not identified. But
without seeing the data, there is no way to tell. What happens if you
constrain the loadings/intercepts to be equal across groups?

Yves.

parts:
I am getting the following error message with this CFA model (ordinal indicators):
 
1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

2: In lav_model_test(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavpartable = lavpartable,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute scaled test statistic
The model involves a large number of resiudal correlations and I am wondering if the large number of parameters being estimated here is partyl the problem. Help would be much appreciated, syntax below:
 

library(lavaan)

model5 <- '

  # measurement model

    calmness =~ state1 + state2 + state5 + state8 + state10 + state11 + state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

    anxiety =~ state3 + state4 + state6 + state7 + state9 + state12 + state13 + state14 + state17 + state18

  # residual correlations for calmness items

state1 ~~ state2 + state5 + state8 + state10 + state11 + state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

state 2 ~~ state5 + state8 + state10 + state11 + state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

state5 ~~ state8 + state10 + state11 + state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

state 8 ~~ state10 + state11 + state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

state10 ~~ state11 + state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

state11 ~~ state15 + state16 + state19 + state20

state15 ~~ state16 + state19 + state20

state16 ~~ state19 + state20

state19 ~~ state20'

 

fit5 <- sem(model5, data = STAI, ordered=c("state1" , "state2" , "state3" , "state4" , "state5" , "state6" , "state7" , "state8" , "state9" , "state10" , "state11" , "state12" , "state13" , "state14" , "state15" , "state16" , "state17" , "state18" , "state19" , "state20"))

 

summary(fit5, fit.measures = TRUE)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Question about the warning message, "lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!"
parts: The model involves a large number of resiudal correlations and I am wondering if the large number of parameters being estimated here is partyl the problem.

That is absolutely the problem.  This model is not identified because all possible residual correlations for all "calmness" indicators are freely estimated, rendering the common factor completely superfluous.  If you suspect many small residual correlations, you probably want to look into using a Bayesian approach with informative priors (an option not yet available using lavaan) -- see the 2012 paper on this web page for details, and the other links on that page provide applied examples:

https://www.statmodel.com/BSEM.shtml

Terry
